equivalent_forms.scope_note: Empirical form with partial orders in several reactants

invariants: Homogeneous of degree ORDER in concentration.
Linear in the rate coefficient at fixed concentration.
Log-log linear: LOG(RATE) is affine in LOG(CONCENTRATION) with slope ORDER.

semantic_interpretation.statement_meaning: The reaction rate is proportional to a power of the reactant concentration, with the exponent fixed by experiment rather than by stoichiometry.
semantic_interpretation.statistical_significance: Chemistry's member of the scaled-power-law family: a symbolic-exponent generalization of the fixed-exponent scaled quadratics and cubics that geometry and mechanics instantiate with ORDER pinned to 2 or 3.
regularity_conditions: Constant temperature so RATECONST is fixed
Order determined empirically for non-elementary steps
failure_modes: Fails when the order changes across the concentration range, as under saturating (Michaelis-Menten) or diffusion-controlled conditions.
The stoichiometric coefficient is not the order except for elementary steps.

provenance.bibliographic_entry: van 't Hoff, J. H. (1884). Etudes de dynamique chimique. Amsterdam: Frederik Muller.
Atkins, P., de Paula, J. (2014). Atkins' Physical Chemistry (10th ed.). Oxford University Press.

equivalent_forms.scope_note: Linearized form used to fit k

invariants: Constant fractional decrement per unit time.
Semilog-linear: LOG(AMOUNT) is affine in TIME with slope -RATECONST.
Scale free in the initial condition: doubling INITIAL doubles AMOUNT at every TIME.
Memoryless: the decay factor over an interval depends only on its length.

symbols.description: Amount (or concentration) remaining at time t.
First-order rate constant, units of inverse time.

functionals.name: exponential
functionals.description: Natural exponential of a dimensionless argument.

semantic_interpretation.statement_meaning: A first-order species decays exponentially: the amount remaining is the initial amount times an exponential factor in the product of rate constant and elapsed time.
semantic_interpretation.statistical_significance: The decay-signed member of the exponential archetype; identical in shape to unconstrained exponential growth in calculus and to radioactive decay, with only the sign of the rate slot distinguishing them.
regularity_conditions: First-order kinetics throughout the observed interval
No back reaction or parallel channel

provenance.bibliographic_entry: Wilhelmy, L. (1850). Ueber das Gesetz, nach welchem die Einwirkung der Saeuren auf den Rohrzucker stattfindet. Annalen der Physik, 157, 413-428.
Atkins, P., de Paula, J. (2014). Atkins' Physical Chemistry (10th ed.). Oxford University Press.

invariants: Independent of the initial amount.
Inversely proportional to the rate constant.
The numerator is dimensionless, so HALFLIFE inherits the reciprocal units of RATECONST.

symbols.description: Time for the amount to fall to one half.

constants.description: Natural logarithm of two; the dimensionless numerator fixed by halving.

semantic_interpretation.statement_meaning: The time to consume half the material is a fixed dimensionless constant divided by the rate constant, and does not depend on how much material was present.
semantic_interpretation.statistical_significance: Joins the ratio archetype of average speed, density and molarity at the shape level but splits from them under typing: its numerator is a constant rather than a measured extensive quantity, which is exactly the initial-amount independence that makes half-life a usable fingerprint.
failure_modes: Constant half-life is diagnostic of first order only; second-order half-life depends on the initial concentration.

provenance.bibliographic_entry: Rutherford, E., Soddy, F. (1903). Radioactive change. Philosophical Magazine, 5(29), 576-591.
Atkins, P., de Paula, J. (2014). Atkins' Physical Chemistry (10th ed.). Oxford University Press.

invariants: Log-linear in reciprocal temperature.
Exponential argument is dimensionless: BARRIER is measured against thermal energy.
Monotone increasing in TEMPERATURE for positive BARRIER.

functionals.name: exponential
functionals.description: Natural exponential of a dimensionless argument.

constants.description: Molar gas constant, shared with the ideal gas law.

semantic_interpretation.statement_meaning: The rate constant rises exponentially with temperature, controlled by the ratio of an activation barrier to the available thermal energy.
semantic_interpretation.statistical_significance: Same exponential envelope as first-order decay, but the exponent is itself a ratio: a Boltzmann-factor archetype shared with any thermally activated process rather than a plain product in the exponent.
regularity_conditions: Single dominant elementary step over the fitted temperature range
failure_modes: Curved Arrhenius plots arise from tunnelling, changing rate-determining steps, or a temperature-dependent pre-exponential factor.

provenance.bibliographic_entry: Arrhenius, S. (1889). Ueber die Reaktionsgeschwindigkeit bei der Inversion von Rohrzucker durch Saeuren. Zeitschrift fuer Physikalische Chemie, 4, 226-248.
Atkins, P., de Paula, J. (2014). Atkins' Physical Chemistry (10th ed.). Oxford University Press.

invariants: Multilinear: absorbance doubles if any single factor doubles.
Additive over independent absorbing species at the same wavelength.
Zero absorbance whenever any factor vanishes.

symbols.description: Molar absorption coefficient at the working wavelength.
Optical path length through the sample.
Amount concentration of the absorbing species.

semantic_interpretation.statement_meaning: Absorbance is the product of a substance-specific absorption coefficient, the optical path length, and the concentration of absorber.
semantic_interpretation.statistical_significance: A trilinear product whose skeleton is that of a rectangular prism's volume: one output measure built from three independent factors. Under typing it sits with the triangle area formula instead, because the absorptivity is a fixed material coefficient in the same slot position that geometry fills with the one-half constant.
regularity_conditions: No photochemistry or saturation of the transition
failure_modes: Linearity breaks above roughly 10 mM through solute-solute interaction and refractive-index change.
Stray light and polychromatic sources bend the calibration curve toward saturation.

provenance.bibliographic_entry: Beer, A. (1852). Bestimmung der Absorption des rothen Lichts in farbigen Fluessigkeiten. Annalen der Physik und Chemie, 86, 78-88.
Bouguer, P. (1729). Essai d'optique sur la gradation de la lumiere. Paris: Claude Jombert.

invariants: Affine in ENTROPY at fixed TEMPERATURE, with slope -TEMPERATURE.
Legendre transform of the enthalpy in the entropy-temperature conjugate pair.
Extensive: scaling the system scales every term but TEMPERATURE.

semantic_interpretation.statement_meaning: The energy available to do non-expansion work is the enthalpy less the part of it bound up by temperature times entropy.
semantic_interpretation.statistical_significance: A signed affine combination: the same skeleton as the statistical affine location-scale map except that the product term enters negated, which is precisely the sign that turns an offset into a trade-off between enthalpy and entropy.
regularity_conditions: Closed system at constant temperature and pressure

provenance.bibliographic_entry: Gibbs, J. W. (1878). On the Equilibrium of Heterogeneous Substances. Transactions of the Connecticut Academy of Arts and Sciences, 3, 108-248, 343-524.
Atkins, P., de Paula, J. (2014). Atkins' Physical Chemistry (10th ed.). Oxford University Press.

invariants: Affine in ENTROPY at fixed TEMPERATURE, with slope -TEMPERATURE.
Legendre transform of the internal energy in the entropy-temperature conjugate pair.
Differs from the Gibbs potential only in which energy term occupies the first slot.

semantic_interpretation.statement_meaning: The energy available to do total work at constant volume is the internal energy less temperature times entropy.
semantic_interpretation.statistical_significance: Exact typed twin of the Gibbs free energy: the two thermodynamic potentials are the same Legendre transform applied to different energy terms, and the matcher recovers that identity from form alone, the way it recovers gravitation from Coulomb.
regularity_conditions: Closed system at constant temperature and volume

provenance.bibliographic_entry: Helmholtz, H. (1882). Die Thermodynamik chemischer Vorgaenge. Sitzungsberichte der Koeniglich Preussischen Akademie der Wissenschaften zu Berlin, 22-39.
Atkins, P., de Paula, J. (2014). Atkins' Physical Chemistry (10th ed.). Oxford University Press.

equivalent_forms.scope_note: Dilute-solution approximation with activity coefficient one

invariants: Order-reversing: greater hydrogen-ion activity gives smaller PH.
Decade-additive: a tenfold change in ACTIVITY shifts PH by exactly one unit.
Argument must be dimensionless (activity, not raw concentration).

symbols.description: Relative activity of the hydrogen ion.

functionals.name: logarithm
functionals.description: Logarithm of a dimensionless argument (base fixed by convention).

semantic_interpretation.statement_meaning: Acidity is reported as the negative logarithm of hydrogen-ion activity, compressing many orders of magnitude onto a small linear scale.
semantic_interpretation.statistical_significance: The generic p-function: a negated logarithmic rescaling that converts multiplicative structure into additive structure, which is what makes every downstream acid-base relation affine rather than multiplicative.
regularity_conditions: Aqueous solution at a stated temperature
Activity referenced to the standard state
failure_modes: The concentration form fails at high ionic strength where activity coefficients depart from unity.

provenance.bibliographic_entry: Sorensen, S. P. L. (1909). Enzymstudien II: Ueber die Messung und die Bedeutung der Wasserstoffionenkonzentration bei enzymatischen Prozessen. Biochemische Zeitschrift, 21, 131-304.
IUPAC (2007). Quantities, Units and Symbols in Physical Chemistry (Green Book, 3rd ed.). RSC Publishing.

invariants: Affine in the logarithm of the base-to-acid ratio, with unit slope.
PH equals PKA exactly when the two species are equimolar.
Invariant under common dilution of both species, since only their ratio enters.

symbols.description: Negative logarithm of the acid dissociation constant.

functionals.name: logarithm
functionals.description: Logarithm of a dimensionless argument (base fixed by convention).

semantic_interpretation.statement_meaning: The pH of a buffer is its pKa displaced by the logarithm of the ratio of conjugate base to weak acid.
semantic_interpretation.statistical_significance: Composition of the ratio archetype inside the p-function: taking logarithms turns a multiplicative equilibrium expression into an offset-plus-log-ratio, the acid-base analogue of any calibration line written on a log axis.
regularity_conditions: Dilute solution with activity coefficients near one
failure_modes: Unreliable when the ratio is far from unity or the acid is not weak, because the approximation that dissociation does not perturb the stated concentrations fails.

provenance.bibliographic_entry: Henderson, L. J. (1908). Concerning the relationship between the strength of acids and their capacity to preserve neutrality. American Journal of Physiology, 21(2), 173-179.
Hasselbalch, K. A. (1917). Die Berechnung der Wasserstoffzahl des Blutes aus der freien und gebundenen Kohlensaeure desselben. Biochemische Zeitschrift, 78, 112-144.

invariants: Intensive quantity formed as the ratio of two extensive quantities.
Invariant under splitting a homogeneous solution into portions.
Undefined in the limit of vanishing volume.

semantic_interpretation.statement_meaning: Molar concentration is the amount of solute divided by the volume of solution that contains it.
semantic_interpretation.statistical_significance: Exact typed twin of average speed and mass density: one extensive quantity per unit of a reference extent. The slots range over different physical dimensions, which is the whole point - the intensive-ratio move is discipline independent.
regularity_conditions: Volume measured for the solution, not the solvent
Stated temperature, since volume is temperature dependent

provenance.bibliographic_entry: IUPAC (2007). Quantities, Units and Symbols in Physical Chemistry (Green Book, 3rd ed.). RSC Publishing.
Atkins, P., de Paula, J. (2014). Atkins' Physical Chemistry (10th ed.). Oxford University Press.
